result.summary: Extends the private broadcast subsystem to support scheduled transaction broadcasts based on block height. Adds a `delay_after_lock_time` parameter to `sendrawtransaction` to hold private broadcasts until the active chain reaches `nLockTime + delay_after_lock_time`. At submission, transactions rejected only with `TX_PREMATURE_SPEND` are accepted into the queue, and are fully re-validated before outbound private connections are initiated at release height.
result.problem: Users who want to broadcast transactions at a specific future block height (such as locktimed transactions) or conceal transaction creation timing must run custom scripts or external schedulers. Submitting future locktime transactions to `sendrawtransaction` today fails validation immediately, and the node offers no mechanism to queue them until they mature.
evidence: Addresses open feature request #34118 ('[feature] Scheduled Transaction Broadcast')
Author states primary goals are convenience and allowing users to 'hide the exact time of the transaction creation (for increased privacy)' by scheduling broadcasts a few blocks into the future
result.scope_notes: Queue state is purely in-memory and lost on node shutdown or crash. Scheduled broadcasts require `-privatebroadcast` and only support height-based locktimes.
result.changed_since_previous: Replaced the previous duration-based parameter (`delay_for`) with randomized time jitter with `delay_after_lock_time`, which schedules releases based on block height (`nLockTime + delay_after_lock_time`). Submission validation was updated to accept transactions that fail ATMP only because of `TX_PREMATURE_SPEND`.
result.card: This PR adds a delay_after_lock_time parameter to sendrawtransaction to schedule private broadcasts for height nLockTime + delay_after_lock_time. Submissions that fail initial mempool validation only due to premature spend (future locktime) are held in memory and re-validated when the release height is reached. This addresses feature request #34118 for scheduling locktimed transactions and decorrelating transaction creation time from broadcast time without external scripts. Pending transactions are not persisted across node restarts.

risk.why: Bugs in validation bypass or scheduled release handling could result in nodes holding or broadcasting invalid transactions or silently dropping transactions without notifying the user.
